scope: Controlled static diagnostic with 16 objects and 24 ideal displacement channels. Boundary geometry is known; E and support stiffness K are unknown. Results do not establish RGB prediction, dynamics, real-material calibration or general boundary learning.
numerical_convergence: All 608 posteriors qualified under unchanged accuracy gates and passed independent audit. The earlier v03 numerical failure is preserved.
physics: All 50 catalog cases qualified before the actual study; all 16 actual objects and 320 recorded physical checks passed.
policy_conclusion: Both proposed and information policies chose the fixed central action at x=0.18 m for every object, family and data law. They exactly tied that fixed baseline. Improvement over random probing does not establish adaptive probing.
uncertainty_conclusion: For matching linear data, initial nominal 90% interval coverage was E=87.5% and K=93.75%. For nonlinear data, central bending changed E coverage from 81.25% to 64.58% and K coverage from 93.75% to 79.17%, while both intervals narrowed. Numerical convergence therefore does not resolve calibration under forward-model mismatch.
statistical_scope: 16 independent object clusters, three reset-noise realizations per action and object, 10,000 paired cluster bootstrap draws. Comparisons are exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.
next_scientific_priority: Use a validated nonlinear forward likelihood or independently calibrated model-discrepancy treatment, then repeat coverage and probing before adding network complexity.
